span.label: Evidence in medical education research falls into four types: quantitative, qualitative, mixed-methods, and design-based research.

span.label: Biomedical evidence hierarchies imported into medical education failed to capture educational relevance and contextual complexity.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: BEME, MERSQI, CASP and realist review frameworks were the appraisal tools most often cited, but they were applied inconsistently across the included studies.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Randomised controlled trials were frequently impractical or educationally reductive in education settings, while qualitative and theory-driven studies were undervalued despite being methodologically rigorous.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Theory is underused throughout the reviewed medical education research and appraisal literature.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The review's product is an integrative appraisal matrix built from the synthesised literature rather than from a single quality score.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The proposed matrix scores studies on six domains - relevance, methodological rigor, theoretical grounding, outcomes meaningfulness, context, and impact - instead of reducing quality to one number.
